title: Neapolitan-Style Pizza Dough
desc: An unbaked pizza foundation with a supple crumb.
steps: Mix flour, yeast and salt. Add water and mix until no dry flour remains.
Knead for 8–10 minutes until smooth and elastic.
Cover and refrigerate for 18–24 hours, allowing room for expansion.
Weigh out the displayed dough yield and reserve any extra. Bring chilled dough to room temperature for 1 hour before shaping; bake according to the finished pizza recipe.

title: Quick Pizza Dough
desc: An unbaked pizza foundation with a supple crumb.
steps: Mix flour, yeast and salt. Add water and mix until no dry flour remains.
Knead for 8–10 minutes until smooth and elastic.
Cover and leave at room temperature for about 1 hour, until doubled.
Weigh out the displayed dough yield and reserve any extra. Bring chilled dough to room temperature for 1 hour before shaping; bake according to the finished pizza recipe.

title: Shortcrust Pastry
desc: A buttery base for pies and quiches.
steps: Mix flour and salt. Rub in cold diced butter until the mixture resembles coarse crumbs.
Add cold water gradually, pressing into a dough; stop once it holds together. Avoid kneading.
Wrap and chill for 30 minutes. Use dusting flour sparingly when rolling.
Weigh out the displayed dough yield; wrap any extra separately. Keep chilled and use within 2 days, or freeze. Follow the finished recipe for shaping and baking.

title: Sweet Tart Pastry
desc: Sweet, crisp pastry for dessert tarts.
ingredients: Eggs, beaten and weighed without shells
steps: Beat softened butter and icing sugar just until smooth, without whipping in much air.
Mix in beaten egg, then flour and salt. Press together gently without kneading.
Flatten, wrap and chill for 1 hour. Roll with a little dusting flour.
Weigh out the displayed dough yield; wrap any extra separately. Keep chilled and use within 2 days, or freeze. Follow the finished recipe for shaping and baking.

title: Pâte Sablée
desc: A tender, crumbly sweet pastry.
steps: Mix flour, icing sugar and salt. Rub in cold diced butter until sandy.
Add yolks and press together gently. Do not knead.
Wrap and chill for 1 hour. Roll between baking paper sheets with a little dusting flour.
Weigh out the displayed dough yield; wrap any extra separately. Keep chilled and use within 2 days, or freeze. Follow the finished recipe for shaping and baking.

title: Rough Puff Pastry
desc: Flaky unbaked pastry with visible butter layers.
steps: Mix flour and salt. Toss in cold butter cubes, flattening them slightly while leaving visible pieces.
Add cold water and press into a rough dough. Wrap and chill for 30 minutes.
On a lightly floured surface, roll into a rectangle three times as long as wide. Fold in thirds, rotate a quarter turn and repeat. Chill for 30 minutes.
Repeat the rolling and folding twice more for four folds in total. Chill for 1 hour; if butter softens at any point, chill before continuing.
Weigh out the displayed dough yield; wrap any extra separately. Keep chilled and use within 2 days, or freeze. Follow the finished recipe for shaping and baking.

title: Classic Puff Pastry
desc: Laminated pastry ready for shaping and baking.
steps: Rub butter into flour and salt, then add cold water. Knead briefly until smooth; wrap and chill for 30 minutes.
Flatten the laminating butter between paper into a square. It must be cool but bend without cracking.
Roll dough on a lightly floured surface into a square large enough to enclose the butter. Place butter diagonally in the centre; fold corners over and seal fully.
Roll into a rectangle three times as long as wide. Brush off excess flour, fold in thirds and rotate a quarter turn. Repeat once, then chill for 30 minutes.
Complete two more pairs of folds, chilling between pairs: six folds altogether. Chill for at least 1 hour before use; keep butter cool throughout.
Weigh out the displayed dough yield; wrap any extra separately. Keep chilled and use within 2 days, or freeze. Follow the finished recipe for shaping and baking.

title: Croissant Dough
desc: Unbaked laminated yeast dough; proof after shaping.
steps: Mix flour, yeast, sugar and salt. Add milk and softened butter; knead for 5 minutes until smooth.
Cover and leave for 1 hour, then flatten, wrap and refrigerate for 8–12 hours.
Flatten laminating butter into a square between paper. Keep it cold but pliable. Roll dough with dusting flour to twice the butter's width and the same height; enclose butter and seal.
Roll the packet into a rectangle three times as long as wide, brush away excess flour and fold in thirds. Rotate a quarter turn and chill for 30 minutes.
Repeat twice more for three folds in total, chilling between folds. Chill for 1 hour. Stop and chill whenever butter softens or dough resists rolling.
Weigh the displayed yield and reserve excess. Keep refrigerated; shape, prove and bake within 1 day using a finished pastry recipe, or freeze the unproofed dough.

title: Danish Pastry Dough
desc: Unbaked laminated yeast dough; proof after shaping.
ingredients: Eggs, beaten and weighed without shells
steps: Mix flour, yeast, sugar and salt. Add milk and beaten egg and softened butter; knead for 5 minutes until smooth.
Cover and leave for 1 hour, then flatten, wrap and refrigerate for 8–12 hours.
Flatten laminating butter into a square between paper. Keep it cold but pliable. Roll dough with dusting flour to twice the butter's width and the same height; enclose butter and seal.
Roll the packet into a rectangle three times as long as wide, brush away excess flour and fold in thirds. Rotate a quarter turn and chill for 30 minutes.
Repeat twice more for three folds in total, chilling between folds. Chill for 1 hour. Stop and chill whenever butter softens or dough resists rolling.
Weigh the displayed yield and reserve excess. Keep refrigerated; shape, prove and bake within 1 day using a finished pastry recipe, or freeze the unproofed dough.

title: Brioche Dough
desc: A rich unbaked dough for shaped sweet breads.
ingredients: Eggs, beaten and weighed without shells
steps: Mix flour, yeast, sugar and salt, then add beaten eggs and milk. Knead for 8 minutes until elastic.
Knead in softened butter in small additions, waiting until each is absorbed. Continue for 10–15 minutes until glossy and stretchy.
Cover and leave for 1½–2 hours until puffy, then gently deflate. Wrap in a roomy container and refrigerate for 8–12 hours.
Weigh out the displayed yield and reserve extra. Shape cold dough and allow to rise again before baking as directed by the finished recipe. Use within 1 day or freeze.

title: Sweet Yeast Dough
desc: A rich unbaked dough for shaped sweet breads.
ingredients: Eggs, beaten and weighed without shells
steps: Mix flour, yeast, sugar and salt, then add beaten eggs and milk. Knead for 8 minutes until elastic.
Knead in softened butter in small additions, waiting until each is absorbed. Continue for 10–15 minutes until glossy and stretchy.
Cover and leave for 1½–2 hours until puffy, then gently deflate. Wrap in a roomy container and refrigerate for 8–12 hours.
Weigh out the displayed yield and reserve extra. Shape cold dough and allow to rise again before baking as directed by the finished recipe. Use within 1 day or freeze.

title: Choux Pastry
desc: Baked hollow shells for profiteroles and cream puffs.
ingredients: Eggs, beaten and weighed without shells
steps: Preheat to 200°C conventional and line trays. Bring water, butter and salt to a full boil.
Add flour all at once and stir vigorously. Cook over medium heat for 2 minutes until dough pulls away from the pan and leaves a thin film.
Transfer to a bowl and stir for 3 minutes to cool. Beat in egg gradually; stop when dough falls slowly from the spoon in a thick V. Reserve any unused egg.
Pipe the displayed number of equal mounds, about 4 cm wide, leaving room to expand. Bake for 20 minutes without opening the door.
Reduce to 170°C conventional and bake for 15–20 minutes until firm and deeply golden. Pierce each shell and return to the switched-off oven for 10 minutes to dry.
Cool completely on a rack. The displayed yield counts baked empty shells ready for filling; freeze unfilled shells if keeping longer than 1 day.

title: Tulip Paste
desc: A thin biscuit paste that can be shaped while hot.
steps: Beat softened butter and icing sugar until smooth.
Mix in egg whites gradually, then fold in flour.
Chill for 30 minutes. Weigh the displayed paste yield and reserve any extra.

For thin decorative biscuits, spread small circles on silicone or baking paper, about 1 mm thick. Bake at 170°C fan for 6–8 minutes until edges are golden; shape over an inverted cup immediately and cool. The yield refers to unbaked paste.

title: Strudel Dough
desc: Stretchable unbaked pastry for strudel.
steps: Mix flour, salt, lukewarm water and oil into a soft dough.
Knead firmly for 10 minutes until very elastic. Cover airtight and rest for 1 hour.
Weigh the displayed yield and reserve extra. Roll on a clean floured cloth, then gently stretch over the backs of your hands until almost transparent.
Trim thick edges and patch small tears with dough. Fill and roll promptly as directed by the finished strudel recipe; do not let the sheet dry out.

title: Filo Dough
desc: Hand-rolled unbaked sheets; keep covered while working.
steps: Mix flour, salt, lukewarm water, oil and vinegar. Knead for 10 minutes until smooth and stretchy.
Cover airtight and rest for 1 hour. Weigh the displayed dough yield and reserve extra.
Divide into small balls. Keep covered while rolling one at a time with cornflour, using a long thin rolling pin, until paper-thin and translucent.
Brush excess cornflour away. Stack sheets between baking paper and cover with plastic so they cannot dry. Use immediately in a finished recipe, brushing fat between layers as that recipe directs.

title: Hot-Water Crust Pastry
desc: A sturdy warm pastry for raised savoury pies.
steps: Mix flour and salt in a heatproof bowl.
Heat water and lard together until melted and just boiling.
Pour into the flour and stir with a spoon. When cool enough to touch, knead briefly until smooth.
Weigh the displayed yield and reserve excess. Shape while warm and pliable; use a finished savoury pie recipe for filling and baking. Keep covered if it must wait briefly.

title: Cookie Crumb Base
desc: A ready-to-press biscuit and butter mixture.
steps: Crush biscuits to fine, even crumbs.
Melt butter gently and stir it through the crumbs.
Mix until the crumbs hold together when squeezed. Weigh the displayed yield and reserve any extra.
Press into the tin specified by the finished recipe. For a chilled dessert, refrigerate for 30 minutes; for a baked base, follow that recipe's oven instructions.

title: Génoise Sponge
desc: An airy egg-foam sponge for layered cakes.
ingredients: Eggs, beaten and weighed without shells
steps: Preheat to 170°C conventional. Line the base and sides of a 20 cm round tin for the base batch; use extra tins for larger batches and a 15 cm tin for a half batch.
Whisk eggs and sugar over barely simmering water until lukewarm, about 40°C. Remove from heat and whisk for 6–8 minutes until thick ribbons hold briefly on the surface.
Sift flour over the foam and fold in gently. Melt butter, cool until warm, mix with vanilla and a spoonful of batter, then fold back into the bowl.
Bake for 25–30 minutes until springy and a skewer comes out clean. Cool for 10 minutes, turn out and cool fully on a rack. The yield counts baked sponge cakes.

title: Joconde Sponge
desc: A thin almond sponge for layered desserts.
ingredients: Eggs, beaten and weighed without shells
steps: Preheat to 190°C fan. Line a 30 × 40 cm shallow tray for the base batch; keep the same batter depth when scaling.
Whisk almonds, icing sugar and whole eggs for 5 minutes until thick and pale. Fold in sifted flour.
In a clean bowl, whisk egg whites to soft peaks, gradually add sugar and whisk to firm peaks. Fold into the almond batter in stages.
Melt butter and cool until warm. Mix with a spoonful of batter, then fold back in and spread evenly in the tray.
Bake for 8–12 minutes until lightly golden and springy. Cool, then peel away the paper. The yield counts baked sheets.

title: Dacquoise
desc: Light hazelnut meringue discs for layered cakes.
steps: Preheat to 150°C fan. Draw two 20 cm circles on baking paper for the base batch, then turn the paper over.
Mix ground hazelnuts and icing sugar, breaking up lumps.
Whisk egg whites to soft peaks. Add sugar gradually and whisk to a firm glossy meringue, then gently fold in the nut mixture.
Pipe or spread inside the circles to an even thickness. Bake for 25–30 minutes until golden and firm, then cool completely before removing paper. The yield counts baked discs.
